# Maersk starts outbound operations at Herleshausen logistics centre
...
Maersk has started outbound operations at its Herleshausen logistics centre. The 71,800m² facility strengthens contract logistics capacity across Germany and neighbouring European markets.
...
- Maersk has started outbound distribution from its new 71,800m² logistics centre in Herleshausen.
- The facility includes 62,800m² of warehouse space and sits directly beside Germany's A4 motorway.
- Employment is expected to reach 300–400 permanent roles, rising to as many as 1,000 people during peak season.

Maersk has started outbound operations from its new logistics centre in Herleshausen, adding 71,800m² of contract logistics capacity in central Germany.

Products have been arriving at the facility since August, while outward distribution has now begun to German and other delivery centres operated by an online retailer. Maersk has leased the building on a long-term basis at Panattoni Park Bad Hersfeld Ost.

The site provides 62,800m² of warehouse space, 2,900m² of offices and 6,100m² of mezzanine floor. Storage racks rise to almost 12 metres, allowing a large quantity of inventory to be held vertically without increasing the building footprint.

Herleshausen sits directly beside the A4 motorway, one of Germany’s principal east-west routes. The location gives the operation access to domestic distribution flows while keeping neighbouring European markets within practical road freight reach.

Ole Trumpfheller, Managing Director of Maersk Area Northern Europe Continent, said: “Herleshausen is the ideal location as a central hub for the flow of goods within Germany and into the neighboring European markets.”
...
Herleshausen adds capacity to Maersk’s wider expansion in contract logistics, where shipping and freight groups are extending further into warehousing and inland distribution. Owning or controlling more stages of a customer’s supply chain can reduce handovers between providers and create a longer operating relationship than a single ocean or road movement.
...
Herleshausen has now crossed from development into live logistics operation. The next measure will come from how reliably Maersk can manage the peak-season swing in labour and volume while maintaining the distribution performance expected from a central European hub.

highlights:
Maersk Invests $100 Million in Massachusetts Fulfillment Hub - Supply Chain 24/7

## The new 617,000-square-foot Maersk fulfillment center will open in late August and create about 1,000 jobs

 

Source: Courtesy of Maersk

Maersk is investing $100 million in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, creating about 1,000 jobs and expanding Northeast delivery capacity.

 By 24/7 Staff July 16, 2026 

Maersk will open a new 617,000-square-foot fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, later this summer, investing $100 million in the project and creating approximately 1,000 jobs.

The facility will become part of Maersk's North American contract logistics network and will work with a major e-commerce customer. At full capacity, the site is expected to process up to 330,000 units a day while expanding the company's fulfillment and delivery network across the Northeast.

The Hopedale facility marks one of Maersk's larger recent investments in U.S. logistics infrastructure as retailers and brands continue placing inventory closer to customers to speed deliveries.

“We are seeing continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities,” said Dave Hune, Head of Maersk Contract Logistics North America. “Our investment in Hopedale reflects continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities and reinforces Maersk's commitment to building resilient, scalable supply chains across North America.”

## Built for high-volume e-commerce

The fulfillment center is equipped with automated conveyor and sortation systems designed to handle large volumes of orders. Maersk said the operation will process up to 330,000 units per day during peak periods.

The site will serve a single large-scale e-commerce customer, although Maersk did not identify the company.

Hiring is already underway for leadership, warehouse, and support positions ahead of the facility's opening later this summer.

## Expanding Maersk's Northeast network

The new operation expands Maersk's contract logistics network in North America and strengthens its presence in the Northeast.

The company said many customers are looking to position inventory closer to consumers to reduce delivery times while improving order fulfillment.

The Hopedale facility combines warehousing, fulfillment, and distribution within Maersk's broader logistics network, which includes ocean shipping, trucking, air freight, and inland transportation.

The company said the investment will help it keep up with customer growth while expanding its fulfillment network in one of the country's largest consumer markets.

highlights:
Parts Town Unlimited has signed a lease for a sprawling 538,450-square-foot distribution facility in Pendergrass, Georgia, a Jackson County town of roughly 500 residents that will soon host the company's largest global fulfillment center. The facility is expected to bring more than 140 team members to the area and is designed to put parts closer to Southeast customers while cutting shipping times and costs.

According to WSB-TV, the warehouse will rely on robotic conveyance and planned AI-powered robotics for packing, shipping and receiving. Parts Town Unlimited signed the full-building lease for Building 1 at Jackson 85 North Business Park, located at 779 Parker Industrial Road, in a deal developed by Trammell Crow Company and joint venture partner CBRE Investment Management, according to Commercial Search. The Class A cross-dock building features 40-foot clear heights, 124 dock doors, four drive-in ramps, 185-foot concrete truck courts, parking for 171 cars and 148 trailers, and a watertight roof already prepped for solar panels, per the same outlet's reporting.
...
The Georgia site will surpass the company's previous largest fulfillment center, a 427,000-square-foot facility in Litchfield Park, Arizona, that opened in December 2024 with an AutoStore system running 85 robots across 60,000 product bins, according to Digital Commerce 360. That Arizona facility was built to handle 4,500 daily orders. Parts Town's distribution network also includes global fulfillment centers in Chicago, Phoenix, and Munich, and the Pendergrass site will be the company's first LEED-certified global fulfillment center, with LEED certification focused on energy efficiency, resource conservation, and healthier indoor environments.

Bill Geary said the new global fulfillment center represents an important next step in the evolution of Parts Town's North American distribution network, and that it will help serve customers and manufacturer partners with greater speed, flexibility, and scale. The company plans to distribute genuine manufacturer parts for commercial foodservice equipment, residential appliances, and HVAC systems out of the new hub, and expects to move in by the end of 2026.

# G10 Fulfillment to Celebrate Grand Opening of New Kenosha Distribution Facility with Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony

 Geneva10 

Sep 01, 2026, 08:34 ET

Mayor and Kenosha County Executive to join company and community leaders in marking the milestone expansion

KENOSHA, Wis., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- G10 Fulfillment, a North American third-party logistics and fulfillment provider, will hold a ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the grand opening of its new distribution facility in Kenosha, Wisconsin, on Thursday, September 10, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. at 12345 38th Street.

The new 315,000-square-foot facility replaces G10's former Twin Lakes location and more than doubles the company's Midwest warehouse capacity. Positioned along the Chicago–Milwaukee freight corridor, the site supports large-scale order fulfillment and regional inventory distribution as part of G10's broader logistics network.

Local officials will join G10 leadership to mark the occasion. Kenosha Mayor David Bogdala and Kenosha County Executive Samantha Kerkmam will offer remarks, with the Kenosha Area Business Alliance (KABA) serving as emcee for the event. Members of the media are welcome to attend.

"This facility represents a major step forward for our Midwest operations," said Mark Becker, CEO of G10 Fulfillment. "Doubling our capacity here in Kenosha allows us to support our retail partners with faster, more reliable fulfillment, and we're proud to be growing alongside a community that has been such a strong partner to our business."

About G10 Fulfillment

Founded in 2009, G10 Fulfillment has grown from a 10,000-square-foot airplane hangar into a multi-node logistics network across the United States. The company combines fulfillment technology with operational expertise to help retail and e-commerce brands—ranging from Walmart and Amazon to fast-growing Shopify companies—manage inventory, shipping and logistics across every sales channel, including regulated hazmat shipping, with speed, accuracy and consistency. For more information, visit https://g10fulfillment.com/.

# Maersk Commits US$100m to New Hopedale Fulfillment Center, Advancing Integrated Logistics Push in the US Northeast

Maersk, the global integrator of container logistics operating across more than 130 countries, is deepening its footprint in North American contract logistics with a US$100m investment in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts. The 617,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to open in late August 2026, positioning the company to strengthen fulfillment capacity for cargo owners across the region.

Built around the requirements of a single major e-commerce customer, the site will function as a central node in Maersk’s contract logistics network throughout the US Northeast. During peak periods, the center is engineered to process up to 330,000 units a day, a throughput enabled by advanced conveyor and sortation systems designed for high-volume, rapid-turnaround operations.

Dave Hune, Head of Maersk Contract Logistics North America, framed the commitment as a direct response to sustained customer demand for modern fulfillment infrastructure. “Our customers continue to seek fulfilment solutions that are resilient and scalable,” Hune said. “This investment reflects our commitment to building supply chains that hold firm through volatility and grow alongside the businesses that depend on them.”

The project also carries substantial employment implications. Close to 1,000 positions — spanning leadership, operations, and support functions — are being filled, with hiring already underway. For the surrounding community, the scale of new employment represents a meaningful economic contribution.

For shippers, the Hopedale centre signals more than added warehouse space. It reinforces Maersk’s broader strategy to unify transportation, warehousing, fulfilment, and distribution into a single integrated logistics proposition for North American customers — an approach designed to reduce hand-off friction, tighten delivery reliability, and give cargo owners greater visibility and control across the supply chain.

The Hopedale investment is not an isolated facility opening. It is evidence of a deliberate strategy to advance end-to-end logistics capability across North America and to help customers navigate demand spikes, cost pressures, and disruption with confidence.

#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

The facility has about 100 workers, a figure he expects to reach 150 by March 2027. Seasonal hiring could push employment toward 200 during the Black Friday peak before tapering in January.

#### G10’s real estate

The move consolidates two smaller warehouses — a 150,000-square-foot building in Twin Lakes and a 50,000-square-foot site in New Berlin — into one operation.

G10 is giving up both former buildings rather than keeping them as backup capacity, according to the chief executive. The company owns the Twin Lakes site, which is being leased to Allied Plastics. The New Berlin property is owned by one of Becker’s business partners and is being turned over to another venture.

Kenosha will be one of three anchor hubs in G10’s national network, he said, alongside a Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, warehouse scheduled to open in October and a planned Ontario, Canada, facility targeted for 2027.

The company is also exploring a location in Southern California.

G10 has grown from a 10,000-square-foot hangar in Lake Geneva in 2009 into a fulfillment operation that stores, processes and ships products for manufacturers and brands across multiple sales channels.

#### Walmart Opens Next-Generation Fulfillment Center in Stockton, Expanding Faster Delivery Across the West Coast 

 Oct. 8, 2026 

#### New facility will create 1,000+ jobs and use advanced automation and technology to increase fulfillment capacity 

 STOCKTON, Calif., Oct. 8, 2026 - Walmart today opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, a more than 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton that will create more than 1,000 jobs and expand the retailer's ability to provide faster shipping and delivery to customers across California and the West Coast. 

 The new facility represents the latest step in Walmart's transformation of its supply chain, bringing associates together with advanced automation, technology and machine learning to move products faster and more efficiently. The technology enables Walmart to materially improve storage capacity and increase the number of customer orders the facility can fulfill each day compared with a traditional fulfillment center. 

 Strategically located in California's Central Valley, the Stockton facility adds significant fulfillment capacity closer to West Coast customers, helping Walmart expand faster shipping options on millions of items while strengthening its broader store and fulfillment network. 

 "This is an exciting day for Stockton and a significant investment in our community," said Timm Quinn, CEO, Stockton Chamber of Commerce. "Walmart's new fulfillment center will create more than 1,000 jobs, bring new career opportunities to our residents and strengthen Stockton's position as a hub for innovation and economic growth in the Central Valley. We're proud to welcome Walmart and look forward to the lasting impact this investment will have on Stockton and the broader San Joaquin County region."

WILMINGTON – Amazon has opened North Carolina’s largest fulfillment center near Wilmington, with more than 1,000 full-time employees at the robotics facility and more than 100 additional jobs at a nearby delivery station.

The company and regional officials marked the opening Oct. 5 at the New Hanover
highlights:
Amazon opens largest NC fulfillment center near Wilmington, adding 1,100 jobs – NC Business Desk
...
WILMINGTON – Amazon has opened North Carolina’s largest fulfillment center near Wilmington, with more than 1,000 full-time employees at the robotics facility and more than 100 additional jobs at a nearby delivery station.

The company and regional officials marked the opening Oct. 5 at the New Hanover-Pender county line. Wilmington Business Development said the two facilities are Amazon’s first direct-to-consumer fulfillment and delivery operations in the Cape Fear region.

The fulfillment center has more than 3 million square feet of operating space across four-and-a-half floors, according to WilmingtonBiz. WECT reported a roughly 650,000-square-foot building footprint and said company officials described it as Amazon’s largest fulfillment center in North Carolina and one of its largest nationwide.
...
The nearby 142,000-square-foot delivery station opened in mid-August at Pender Commerce Park and is expected to create more than 100 jobs. Together, the fulfillment center and delivery station add at least 1,100 direct jobs to the region.
...
The project also closes a multiyear development cycle. WilmingtonBiz reported that a developer representing Amazon withdrew from a purchase contract for the former BASF vitamin-plant site in early 2022. Amazon later bought the property in August 2024, and construction began a few months afterward. An interlocal agreement between New Hanover and Pender counties coordinated planning and permitting across the county line.

The completed operations give southeastern North Carolina a new large-scale logistics employer and shorten the distance between regional customers and Amazon inventory. The combination of more than 1,100 jobs, high-volume processing and a holiday-season ramp makes the opening a material operating milestone rather than a proposed development.
